items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: after Maxine Sullivan started singing with them

ctx.x: in there, you know. But these are the days when -- nobody really made any money. Nat Cole was in it, playing intermissions down there with his little group, didn't make anything. Nobody -- money's just something you didn't -- you couldn't make, so you didn't even think about it. You just played because you loved to play back at that time, you know.

Every once in a while a guy would break loose and do a little something and make a little something for himself. Kirby -- I think that band finally did get to making a little money, not a lot, John Kirby's band, because they caught on on recordings after a while around, and that was after Maxine Sullivan started singing with them, you know, because Kirby was married to her at one time. John Kirby was married to her.

But New York was a fun spot. This was a fun place. You wouldn't want to be anywhere else then because everything happened there. And all the bands that were on the road, they were just aching to get back to New York, not to make money, but where all the action was, you know? And it was really there.
